title: Marginal vs effective tax rates
concept: Your marginal rate is what you pay on the next dollar you earn. Your effective rate is your total tax divided by income — usually lower. People mix these up and make weird decisions about overtime or raises.
takeaway: A raise still increases your take-home pay. Marginal brackets apply slice by slice.

scenario.situation: You might move into a higher federal bracket. A friend says you'll 'lose money' if you earn more.

choices.text: Decline the raise to stay in the lower bracket
Take the raise — only income inside the new bracket is taxed at that rate
Quit working November 1 to avoid taxes

feedback.A: Brackets aren't cliffs. More income means more money in your pocket overall.
feedback.B: Correct. Progressive tax applies marginally, not to every dollar retroactively.
feedback.C: Taxes are a cost of earning — earning zero to avoid them is a losing trade.

scenario.lesson: Understand marginal vs average before negotiating pay.

title: Withholding is not your final tax bill
concept: Employers withhold taxes from paychecks as estimates. Your actual liability is settled at tax time with deductions and credits. A big refund means you gave the government an interest-free loan.
takeaway: Tune withholding if refunds or bills are extreme.

scenario.situation: You get a $3,200 refund every spring and treat it like a bonus.

choices.text: Adjust W-4 so more money hits your paycheck; save intentionally
Stop filing taxes since you already paid withholding

feedback.A: It works, but you could earn or pay down debt with that cash all year.
feedback.B: Correct. Better cash flow plus your own savings account beats a free loan to Uncle Sam.
feedback.C: Filing reconciles liability — skipping is not a strategy, it's a problem.

scenario.lesson: Aim for small refunds or small balances owed.

title: Deductions vs credits (credits win)
concept: Deductions reduce taxable income. Credits reduce tax dollar-for-dollar. A $1,000 credit is usually worth more than a $1,000 deduction for most people.
takeaway: Hunt credits first when you read tax software summaries.

scenario.situation: You qualify for a $1,500 tax credit and could also take a $1,500 deduction.

choices.text: Prioritize the credit — it cuts tax directly
Skip both to keep the return simple

feedback.A: Credits and deductions move different levers — credits are usually stronger.
feedback.B: Correct. Credits are the heavy hitters for lowering what you owe.
feedback.C: Simple is nice, but leaving money on the table is expensive.

scenario.lesson: Know which line items are credits vs deductions.

title: 401(k) and the tax break basics
concept: Traditional 401(k) contributions often lower taxable income now; money grows tax-deferred. Roth 401(k) uses after-tax dollars but can grow tax-free for qualified withdrawals. Both beat not investing for retirement.
takeaway: At minimum, capture any employer match — that's part of your pay.

scenario.situation: Your employer matches 50% up to 6% of salary. You're not contributing yet.

choices.text: Wait until you understand every investment option perfectly
Contribute at least 6% to get the full match
Skip retirement — you'll earn more later

feedback.A: Perfection is the enemy of free money. Start simple, improve later.
feedback.B: Correct. The match is a guaranteed return you can't replicate elsewhere.
feedback.C: Later never gets cheaper — compounding rewards early starters.

scenario.lesson: Free match first, optimize fund choices second.

title: Estimated taxes for side income
concept: If you earn money outside a W-2 job, no one may be withholding for you. You might owe quarterly estimated taxes to avoid penalties — especially if side income grows.
takeaway: Set aside a slice of every freelance payment for taxes.

scenario.situation: You start freelancing and earn $800/month extra with no withholding.

choices.text: Spend it all — taxes sort themselves out
Save ~25–30% for taxes and learn quarterly deadlines
Hide the income from your accountant

feedback.A: April surprises hurt. Side income still counts.
feedback.B: Correct. A simple tax bucket prevents panic and penalties.
feedback.C: Honest reporting keeps sleep and avoids bigger problems.

scenario.lesson: Self-employed cash flow includes a silent partner: taxes.
